suite_notes: The ANSWER half of the analytics gate: the verbatim question text the chat-path gate runner sends, one entry per section of ground-truth/EXPECTED.md. This file is the only place a gate question is defined — scripts/analytics_gate_run.py reads it and records its git blob sha in the run document, so a score is reproducible and a reworded question shows up as a diff instead of as a regression. Do NOT confuse it with ../tool-selection/analytics-gate.json, which scores which TOOLS get selected for a similar-looking utterance and carries ids in the same qNN space; the cross-link is tool_selection_fixture_id on each entry.

chat_path_gate.rationale: Every question whose serving endpoints have shipped (Wave 1 and Wave 2, analytics-capability-plan.md §3/§4) AND whose ground truth is computable on the TRACKB seed AND whose Wave 2 call count is inside its §6 budget. The other eight are excluded for a stated reason on their own entry — an unbuilt Wave 3 composition, an over-budget Wave 2 loop, or a BLOCKED ground truth. The set is the Wave 2 exit gate (docs/gate-runs/wave-2/README.md) plus Wave 1's q13.

window_shapes.calendar: Whole calendar periods ending with the last COMPLETE one (SystemPromptDefaults window rules, #1661/#1670).
window_shapes.rolling: The period ending on the as-of date.
window_shapes.point-in-time: A balance or state measured at the as-of instant; no range.
window_shapes.mixed: Two independent conditions in one question that keep different shapes.

questions.utterance: Who were our top customers by revenue over the last twelve months compared with the twelve months before that?

window.notes: QUESTION/GROUND-TRUTH GAP. `over the last twelve months` reads ROLLING, and the comparison phrase `the twelve months before that` names no calendar period, so the #1670 mixed-comparison precedence does not fire and both windows read rolling — while the ground truth measures both on the calendar. With EVAL_AS_OF on a month boundary the two readings differ only at the endpoints, so the gap has not yet moved a score (q07 DEFLECTed on 2026-09-03). Resolve by restating to `in the last twelve months compared with the twelve months before that` when the question is next revised.

expected.note: Left unset deliberately. This question's own note says the mixed-comparison precedence does NOT fire here — 'over the last twelve months' reads ROLLING and 'the twelve months before that' names no calendar period — so under the shipped DATE_WINDOW contract both windows read rolling. An expectation of CALENDAR_SPAN would fail a contract-correct answer. Annotate once the utterance is restated to name the shape it wants; the comparison is also PRIOR_PERIOD, not YEAR_EARLIER.

A ROLLING resolution must FAIL here: it is the backward window, and the two were indistinguishable while this was unset.

questions.utterance: Which vendors have increased their average bill amount by more than 10% year over year?

window.notes: OPEN QUESTION/GROUND-TRUTH GAP — the same defect class #1671 fixed on q09, left open deliberately. The question names no window at all; `year over year` says only that two equal periods are compared. The ground truth inherits q15's six-month windows because both are served by the same E8 call, which is an implementation accident, not something the question says. Any score on q17 is therefore conditional on the grader accepting those windows. Fixing it means either restating the question with an explicit period or restating EXPECTED.md Q17 against a twelve-month year-over-year comparison; that choice interacts with the q15/q17 reading corrected by #1670 and is tracked separately.

expected.note: Left unset deliberately. This question's own note records that it names no window, that the six-month windows are an implementation accident rather than something the question says, and that any score on it is conditional. Annotating it would convert an acknowledged ground-truth gap into binding ground truth.
